I passed by this store and saw it so often that I was curious, but it didn't really appeal to me, so I didn't stop by for a while, but it was hot today, so I wanted something cool, so I stopped by.

I knew the salt flavor was famous, but there weren't many different types of ice cream in the refrigerated showcase, and when I asked if tasting was possible, I was told that it wasn't possible. I was a little confused as to whether there were places in the ice cream shop where tasting was not possible, but I couldn't see anything that seemed curious about the color of the ice cream, so I just asked for one scoop of the salt flavor, which seems to be the representative menu item.

No matter what size of ice cream I ordered, it seemed like they gave me a spoonful of any other flavor I wanted in addition to the ice cream I ordered, so I asked the clerk serving the ice cream which was better, the cocoa flavor next to the salt flavor or the misut powder flavor, and he said that he personally liked the misut powder flavor, so I asked for the misut powder flavor.

First, you pay, and the clerk skillfully fills the ice cream into a cute-sized cup in several batches and hands it to you.

The store had tables in a relatively large space if you went up about half a flight of stairs.

I first tasted the rice flour-flavored ice cream on a spoon, hoping to see what it would taste like. It wasn't particularly rich or impressive, and had a mild taste, so I didn't find it particularly attractive. When I tasted the main salt-flavored ice cream, I couldn't help but wonder what ice cream with the right viscosity tasted like, but the taste that gradually came to mind was coffee creamer or baby powder.

I can't really taste the salt, but maybe it's because of the salt, but the sweetness isn't too much, so it feels attractive in its own way.

After I finished eating, I drank the slightly melted ice cream left in the cup, and now I could clearly feel the subtle saltiness.

Overall, it seems to be a fairly famous store, but I passed by it often but had no intention of stopping by. It was a hot day today, so I stopped by spontaneously. The salt-flavored ice cream seemed to have its own charm, but I couldn't taste it, and it didn't have the unique taste of Sticky Ricky in Huam-dong, so it was okay.

reviews.text:
I wanted to go to Scent Grill BBQ in the evening, but my family didn't want to go out, so I had no choice but to bring it late last night, but no one was full, so I warmed up the fried chicken I had saved, and after eating it, I was full and I didn't seem to have walked much today, so I wanted to go for a walk, but this agagelato posted by Hyunseo caught my eye.

I like ice cream and cold things, so I still drink coffee or pink lemonade at home every day, and when I finish drinking it, I chew on the ice cubes in the cup. It's not like I go out to an ice cream shop on purpose, but if there's a good restaurant, I stop by whenever I get the chance. It's been a while since I've been to a gelato shop, so I leave my house to stop by because it's reasonably close.

I think it closes at 6 on Sundays, but I left home a little after 5 and walked about 20 minutes to arrive in front of the store.

It was close to closing time, so I approached the front of the store thinking that maybe it had already closed because there were no customers or that it would be busy, but... it was quite crowded, so it was more popular than the popular Kagenga.

When I entered the store, the female salesperson was wearing a mask and gestured to ask if I would like to try a sample. After looking at the menu, she said that she wanted to choose two flavors and asked if sampling was possible. When I looked at the flavors, I saw that it was a gelato shop, not an American ice cream shop like Sticky Ricky in Huam-dong. It was made up of flavors similar to what you would find at a typical gelato shop, with fresh natural ingredients rather than unique flavors. I sampled several flavors, and among them, fresh basil milk seemed to be my type the most. I chose salty crackers.

The female salesperson told me to choose one of the four flavors on the far right of the refrigerated showcase as a service, and that she would add one more as a sample. Lotus is a very familiar taste, but I still ask for Lotus.

There wouldn't be many seats in the store because there were family customers, so I decided to eat outside the store. I brought out the gelato and tried the Lotus at the top, which I had already sampled. It was a taste I knew too well, but I didn't feel anything special. When I tasted the salty cracker, which is the gelato at the top, it reminded me of the salt-flavored ice cream from Garosu-gil Uyuni Ice Cream, but the salt-flavored ice cream there doesn't seem to have that much of a salt taste when I eat it. If you felt salty, this is good because you can immediately feel the subtle saltiness, and the texture of the gelato is fresh and light compared to regular milk, such as the organic milk fish that I felt in the past with Pasteur milk. It is not creamy because it contains a lot of milk and not much cream, but it has the cool particle feel that I expect from ice cream, so it is nice because it exudes a fresh feeling.

Next, I tasted the fresh basil milk, which was the gelato below that I liked more. I liked the light particle feel of the light and cool gelato, and most of all, I liked the freshness of the natural ingredients and the fragrant basil scent as it had fine basil leaves.

Instead, since it has such a light and fresh texture, it almost feels like it's melting like snow, disappearing around the throat without feeling like something went into the stomach, so even if it's not full, it barely feels like you've eaten something, so it feels a bit empty.

I quickly finished eating and was heading home when I felt a small foreign body in my mouth or throat. I thought about what it was and realized that all the basil leaf particles seemed to be stuck instead of going over.

The freshness of raw basil leaves is good, but it would be nice if the size of the basil leaf particles that stick to the inside of the mouth or throat gradually improves.

As I was walking home, I stopped by Cafe Noted, which seemed to be popular for its donuts. I originally thought it was an Instagram-style store that didn't suit me, but when I saw the donuts on display through the long waiting line, I wasn't immediately drawn to it, so I decided to try it out next time I got a chance.

As I wanted to go for a walk, I happened to see a review posted by Hyunseo and stopped by for a quick stroll not far from my house. The agagelato here had a feeling of natural ingredients, similar to other gelato shops, but the light texture with a fresher, grainy feel was a good experience. I liked that I could taste almost everything without any restrictions on sampling. It was a visit that made me want to stop by again next time when I get the chance and try other flavors with seasonal ingredients.

'Is it that special?' A Japanese-style shortcake that always comes to mind.
--------
※ Digression - History of the name ‘Shortcake’
It's been over hundreds of years since the word 'Shortcake' was coined, but the shortcake of that time was different from the whipped cream cake we know. 'Shortbread' or 'Shortcake' is a traditional Scottish biscuit that has existed since before the 12th century, and short is a word used in Scotland to mean 'easy to crumble'. In the case of shortbread, it is quite different from today's shortcake because it is not raised with baking powder.

Modern shortcakes made with baking powder have been popular in the United States since the 1800s. Among them, 'Strawberry shortcake' is a dessert with strawberries and whipped cream sandwiched between shortcakes, and has become the most widely known and popular dish using shortcakes. In other words, a shortcake in the West is a puffed biscuit or a dessert made using it.

Strawberry shortcake was also spread to Japan, and there were major changes along the way. Biscuits were replaced with sponge cakes. As this type of strawberry shortcake became popular, the meaning of shortcake naturally solidified in Japan as 'sponge cake topped with fruit and whipped cream.' Likewise in Korea, when you think of whipped cream cake, Japanese shortcakes often come to mind.

Through this process, a fluffy cake that does not fit its name of breaking easily was born.

Perhaps because it was strawberry season, cakes made with strawberries were the main lineup.

In the case of Strawberry Shoto, since it is a very popular cake, it didn't deviate much from expectations, but the quality is really great. Both the whipped cream and the sponge are really moist and soft without any greasy or crumbly feeling. When cutting, there is almost no resistance like acorn jelly.

Chocolate Strawberry Shoto is similar in composition to Strawberry Shoto, but the difference is that it uses chocolate sponge cake and chocolate sheets. A bit of chocolate flavor is added to the strawberry shoto, giving it a richer taste.

Choco Banana Shoto is significantly different from the previous two. It uses chocolate cream and has banana and chocolate crunch in between. The bananas were really ripe and blended well with the chocolate cream without any interference. It was nice because it felt like it was one ingredient from the beginning rather than feeling like I was eating the banana and cream separately. The most delicious cake out of the three.
--------
Since whipped cream cake itself is a common dessert, and the ingredients are not very diverse or the taste is not unusual, it may not be as impressive as you think. However, you can immediately tell that the quality of the cream and bread is excellent, and the fact that it has such a good balance proves that it is a great dessert... If you haven't tried it, I recommend you go.

Recommendation: ★★★★☆

When it comes to McDonald's burgers, I like the Big Mac. I read an online article recently and it said that the CEO of McDonald's Korea has recently changed and the burger buns have gotten better than before and they are getting a good response from consumers. I was curious to see what the pear chiller that came out after the CEO changed would feel like so I stopped by.

I decided to try the Big Mac, which was said to have a different bun, next time and ordered a pear chiller at the kiosk. There were three sizes, so I ordered a small size to just taste it for now and eat it at the store.

After waiting for a while, my order number finally came up and I went to pick it up, but instead of the common plastic cup I was expecting, it was a hard plastic cup with only a plastic lid covering it. I understand the situation at the store, but it was an ugly cup rather than a pretty glass or plastic cup, so just looking at it already made me feel tasteless.

When I tried the pear chiller using a straw and used domestically produced Naju pears, it was good to feel the particles of the pear, but it felt like there was too much syrup, so it was the sweetness of the syrup rather than the clear refreshing sweetness of the pear. Although it was refreshing because it was a chiller, it did not taste refreshing, but just felt cold, so I was quickly disappointed.

I was curious about what a pear chiller would feel like. I like the idea of ​​making pears into a chiller, but I don't know if pear is a fruit that is particularly suitable as a chiller.

Overall, I wish the previous Big Mac had a little more sauce or lettuce, but I didn't have any major complaints. I heard that the quality has improved since the CEO of McDonald's Korea changed, so even though it's not a Big Mac, I was curious about what the new menu item, Pear Chiller, felt like, so I stopped by and tasted it, but I was disappointed because it felt like the refreshing sweetness of Korean Naju pears were not properly utilized due to the excessive syrup, so it felt like the characteristics of Naju pears were not utilized well.

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
Among the burgers I encountered as a child, the one that left the most impression on me was probably the fish burger I enjoyed eating at Americana, which was located on the first basement level of the former Woosung Shopping Center at Seoi Elementary School intersection in Seocho-dong.

Of course, I liked the Yankee Burger with the beef patty, but I think I liked the fish burger more, and I can still feel the taste from back then.

Ever since I was young, I liked salty food rather than sweet food, but I liked American chains like McDonald's, Burger King, and Wendy's, but I've never liked Lotteria.

Additionally, when I was young, I was very sensitive to meat and would barely eat anything other than ground beef, so there may be a reason why I can comfortably eat a fish burger with fish in it.

So, I have good memories of the fish burger, and I heard that McDonald's is re-releasing the discontinued fish burger, Filet O' Fish. I think I must have tasted the Filet O Fish once or twice a long time ago before it was discontinued. Considering that I barely remember it, I don't think it had an impressive taste, but I was still excited to try it again, so I stopped by as a snack before dinner.

When I arrived at McDonald's and ordered the Filet O' Fish as a single item, I asked for a little more tartar sauce. I was told that I could leave out the sauce but not add more. What was this situation? I thought that was the policy, so I said I knew and waited, and after waiting a bit, my order number came up, so I went to the counter and got the Filet O Fish.

When I opened the packaging, I saw that the relatively small Filet O Fish had a fairly thick cod patty and cheese.

When I grabbed the filet o' fish and took a bite, it was so bland that I understood why I couldn't remember anything I had tasted before.

I heard that the bun had been upgraded before, so I stopped by and tried the Big Mac out of curiosity. It didn't feel like it was in harmony with the whole, but felt disparate, so I was disappointed because I felt like the old bun was better. However, the steamed bun was moist, contrary to expectations, but the texture and taste were not good because the outer crust of the bun and the inner bread were integrated. On the contrary, the outer crust felt subtle and was not moist enough, so it was a bit stiff, so I was disappointed.

The cod patty is thick, but the batter on the patty doesn't have a special texture and I can barely feel it, and the flavor of the cod meat is also plain. I desperately need help from the tartar sauce, but I can't feel it. When I'm wondering when I'll feel it, I finally feel the taste of the tartar sauce with the slightly sour pickles. I wonder if I've finally been saved, but as I worried, there's too little of it, so I thought I could finally feel it now, but I can't feel it again any time soon. If I wanted to eat it the way I like it, I feel like I should have added at least three times as much.

Overall, I was curious about McDonald's Filet O' Fish, which was re-released as it reminded me of the Americana fish burger I loved when I was young, so I stopped by on the release date and tried it. I was disappointed because it tasted bland, but it's better to have an option to choose from, so I don't mind if it disappears again.

However, McDonald's believes that the Big Mac is the truth.
